extracted.intended_audience: members of the Royal Society, natural philosophers, physicians and surgeons (17th-century scientific readership)
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of evaluative criteria and procedural standards embedded in a Philosophical Transactions page containing a transfusion case report, an anatomical (hermaphrodite) description, short book notices, an optics report, tide observations, and a list of inquiries/directions for the Antilles. Focus is on the standards, observations, and requirements the text uses to judge, perform, or request scientific/medical work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indication and patient selection for transfusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Decision to attempt transfusion after other remedies (bleeding, bathing, potions) failed; chosen because prior experiments suggested no danger and calf's blood might allay 'heat and ebullition' of patient's blood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider patient history (recurrent, long-lasting phrenzy), prior treatments and their effects; weigh experimental evidence and observers' experience before attempting transfusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfusion operation protocol and technique
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure described: open crural artery of a calf; draw about ten ounces from patient's arm (right arm first), convey calf blood via pipe into patient's veins; manage posture and crowd to allow adequate flow; stop if patient swoons; close wounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform in presence of experienced physicians; use an assistant/keeper familiar with prior experiments; monitor for swooning and stop inflow; adjust volumes based on patient's thinness and condition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dosage and repetition considerations for transfusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial transfusion small (patient ~10 oz bled, received ~5–6 oz calf blood); second transfusion larger (overall patient received more than one whole pound considering calf residue); effect faster and greater with larger transfusion; a third transfusion sometimes considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust withdrawn and infused volumes to patient's constitution; expect dose–response (larger transfusion → quicker more marked effects); consider repeating but proceed cautiously given uncertainty/risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate physiological signs to monitor during transfusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Patient reported heat along the arm and under the armpits, rising and varying pulse, plentiful sweat, kidney and stomach pains, tendency to faint/urge to choke; vomiting and subsequent relief; urgency to urinate and stool; eventual sleep.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record sensations, pulse changes, diaphoresis, visceral complaints, emesis, diuresis and defecation as indicators of reaction to transfusion; be prepared to halt infusion if severe distress occurs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-transfusion outcome measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Observed post-op improvements: sleep uninterrupted, calmer actions and words, restored presence of mind, normalized urine color over days, decreased extravagancies, capacity to make confession and receive Communion, wife's and physicians' testimony of restored condition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use behavioral, physiological (sleep, urine color), social (family testimony) and clerical/medical attestations as combined evidence of improvement; remain cautious about longer-term relapse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for witnesses and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Operation performed in presence of many persons of quality and several physicians and surgeons to avoid suspicion and to be able to testify that there was 'no danger' and to validate effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct novel or risky procedures in front of credible witnesses and record their names and observations to support claims of safety and efficacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cautions and risk acknowledgement for transfusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors claim operation is 'in itself incapable of causing the death of any one, if discreetly managed' but confess insufficient experience to promise cure for such madness; footnote later notes a third transfusion terminated fatally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State limitations of experience and be explicit about observed and later adverse outcomes; counsel caution and further observation before drawing strong conclusions about efficacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anatomical and behavioral diagnostic features for hermaphrodite description
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed morphological criteria: presence of testes (large, in scrotal-like cutaneous folds with hair), labia-like structures formed from testicular production, intact nymphae and myrtiform carunculae, membranous covering of the vulva, absent clitoris, a penis ~4 inches erect with an imperforate glans (membrane potentially puncturable), history of menstruation for two years beginning about age 16 then cessation with beard and hair growth, virile voice and habitus, preference for women and erection on seeing women while flaccid for men.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine external genital anatomy, secondary sexual characteristics, developmental history (menstruation onset/cessation), and sexual behavior/preferences when characterizing intersex individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Components to distinguish in doctrine of percussion (book-evaluation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Aspects to be accurately distinguished in percussion: the percussive force, the motion/velocity of the percussion, and the resistance of the percussed body; an estimate of the proportion of those three to one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A rigorous treatise should define and demonstrate those distinctions and their proportions; relate percussion to gravity, magnetism, tremor, pendulums, etc., and attempt formal demonstration (as Borelli claims).

rubrics_metrics.name: Optics lens-evaluation criteria (non-spherical figures)
rubrics_metrics.description: New non-spherical ocular lenses evaluated by: taking in a greater angle, representing objects more exactly in their respective proportions, bearing a greater aperture free from colours compared to a common spherical telescope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare new lens designs against good spherical instruments for field of view, proportional representation, chromatic aberration and effective aperture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reading-glass performance criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: A reading-glass of the new non-spherical figure 'magnified the letters ... up to the very edges' and showed them distinctly across the whole brim, whereas a spherical glass did not; but the new figure performed best only on one side.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess reading-glasses by uniformity of magnification across the lens, edge-to-edge clarity, and side-to-side symmetry of performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burning-glass performance and focus criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Burning concave glasses evaluated by diameter and focal length: ability to warm faces at four to five feet, burn gloves/garments at ~three feet, and ignite wood within five to ten seconds under suboptimal (gloomy) conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report diameter, focal distance and observed heating/ignition times under specified conditions; note dependence on ambient light and weather.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thermal collection and storage observation for lenses
rubrics_metrics.description: Observation that a concave lens exposed to a northern window (little direct sun) collected warmed air during the day and could warm a hand, but did not do so after sunset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note effects that persist beyond direct solar illumination (thermal storage) versus transient focusing; differentiate daylight thermal collection from post-sunset performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tidal observation: diurnal variation rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Diurnal tides from late March to late September are about a foot higher in the evening than in the morning (i.e., tides after noon and before midnight higher); the reverse holds from Michaelmas to Lady-day (morning tides higher by ~1 foot).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting local tides, specify seasonal diurnal asymmetry and quantify approximate differences; allow for proportional scaling to other places.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tidal observation: timing of highest monthly spring tide
rubrics_metrics.description: The highest monthly spring tide is always the third tide after the new or full moon, unless opposed by a cross wind (e.g., north-east or north-west).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When predicting monthly highest springs, consider lunar phase sequence and wind conditions as modifying factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tidal velocity pattern
rubrics_metrics.description: Water velocity increases with the tide until mid-water (half flood), at which time velocity is strongest, then decreases proportionally until high water.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record velocity vs. tidal phase and note the point of maximum velocity around mid-flood; use such patterns in schemes of tidal progression for a locality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antilles inquiry 1: junipa fruit dye and animal tinting
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the juice of the fruit of the tree junipa, being as clear as rock water, yields a brown violet dye that upon twice application looks black, disappears in nine or ten days, cannot be removed with soap, and whether animals (hogs, parrots) eating the fruit have flesh and fat tinged violet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antilles inquiry 2: acomas fruit effect on ring doves
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether ring doves that feed upon the bitter fruit of the acomas tree have their flesh bitter also.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antilles inquiry 3: properties of acajou wood
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the wood of the acajou tree, being red, light and well scented, never rots in water nor breeds worms when cut in due season, and whether chests/trunks made of it keep clothes from being worm-eaten.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antilles inquiry 4: Indian wood leaves as seasoning
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the leaves of a certain tree called Indian wood give a haut-gout to meat and sauces like a composition of several spices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antilles inquiry 5: soap-wood species and uses
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether there are two sorts of the wood called saponier or soap-wood, one whose fruit serves for soap and the other whose root does so.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antilles inquiry 6: paretuvier-wood bark tanning quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the bark of the paretuvier-wood tans as well as oak-bark.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antilles inquiry 7: laitus root effect on fish
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the root of the tree laitus, when brayed and cast into rivers, makes fishes drunk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antilles inquiry 8: manioc yield per acre
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the root of the manioc is so fertile that one acre planted therewith yields enough to feed more people than six acres of the best wheat.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antilles inquiry 9: manioc toxicity symptoms
rubrics_metrics.description: What symptoms usually follow on taking the juice of manioc, or eating juice with the root, and what effects infer it to be accounted a rank poison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antilles inquiry 10: palmetto royal timber qualities
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the palmetto royal is very tall, straight, tough, not blown down or hollow, and suitable for long optic tubes; request for largest pieces to be sent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antilles inquiry 11: ricinus (palma Christi) oil against vermin
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the oil expressed from the plant ricinus (palma Christi) is used by the Indians to keep them from vermin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antilles inquiry 12: sensitive trees on isthmus
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether there is a wood full of sensitive trees on the isthmus from Nombre de Dios to Panama whose leaves and branches move and fold together with a rattling noise when touched.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antilles inquiry 13: purgative fruit kernels like Jordan almond
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether certain kernels of a fruit like a white pear plum are very purgative and emetic, but if the thin film dividing them is removed they are sweet like Jordan almonds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antilles inquiry 14: 'herbe aux fleches' (dart-herb) for poisoned wounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Request to send roots of the herb called 'herbe aux fleches' which, when stamped, is said to have virtue of curing wounds made with poisoned darts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antilles inquiry 15: specimen of musk-grain
rubrics_metrics.description: To send some of the grain of the herb musk carefully packed so it may keep its musk scent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antilles inquiry 16: specimen collection of medicinal herbs
rubrics_metrics.description: To send specimens of all medicinal herbs with their reputed virtues, including prickle-with, mastic-tree, locust, black-wood, yellow within, five-sprig, tidle-wood, white-wood, Barbadoes-cedar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antilles inquiry 17: mancenille fruit and milky juice hazards
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the mancenille fruit is fatal to the eater, kills fish in water, and whether its milky white juice is dangerous (burning on shirt, swelling on flesh, temporary blindness if in eye), whether its shadow is noxious, and whether natives use its juices in arrow poisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antilles inquiry 18: tatou skin and tail bone medicinal/defensive claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the skin of the tatou and the little bone in its tail cure deafness and ear-pains, and whether the animal is proof against dog bites and bullets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antilles inquiry 19: 'canides' birds docility and vocal mimicry
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether birds called canides are so docile that some learn to speak Indian, Dutch and Spanish and sing airs in the Indian tongue; and whether the colibry has a scent as sweet as amber and musk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antilles inquiry 20: fregati bird fat medicinal uses
rubrics_metrics.description: To procure fat of birds called fregati reputed to be anti-paralytical and anti-podagrical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antilles inquiry 21: land-pike specimen request
rubrics_metrics.description: To send over a land-pike said to be like the water pike but with four feet by which it crawls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antilles inquiry 22: sea wolf (requiem) skin uses and guided fish
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether sea wolf skin is so rough/stiff that files are made of it, and whether it is guided by another fish adorned with curious colours (necklaces of pearls etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Antilles inquiry 23: sea calf (lamantin) skin hardness
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether sea calf skins, when dried, are so hard the Indians use them for shields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antilles inquiry 24: ashes of freshwater tortoises for hair loss
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether ashes of freshwater tortoises, powdered, hinder falling of the hair.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antilles inquiry 25: land crabs underground moulting behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether land crabs hide underground for about six weeks at certain times and renew their shells during that time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antilles inquiry 26: venom correlation with snake coloration
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether snakes with black and white spots on their backs are non-venomous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antilles inquiry 27: ouayamaca lizard skins with metallic scales
rubrics_metrics.description: Request to send skins of large lizards called ouayamaca (up to five feet) especially those with scales so bright they resemble cloth of gold and silver.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antilles inquiry 28: shining flies (cucuyes) light behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether shining flies called cucuyes hide most of their light when taken but afford it plentifully when at liberty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antilles inquiry 29: bees producing black wax and white sweet honey
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether there are bees brown and blue that make a black wax but whose honey is whiter and sweeter than European honey.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antilles inquiry 30: indigenous snake-bite cures
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether Indians cure serpent bites by eating fresh citron pills and applying an unguent made of the bruised head of the wounding serpent hot upon the wound.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antilles inquiry 31: woodlice (and remedy) destructive behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether woodlice generated from rotten wood can eat through trunks in a day or two and spoil linen, clothes and books (spare only written/printed matter), and gnaw supports so cottages fall; and whether remedies include turning the fixed wood ends in ground or rubbing wood with palma Christi oil.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antilles inquiry 32: ravets vermin material preferences
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the vermin called ravets spare nothing they meet (paper, cloths, linen, woollen) except silk and cotton.
